text: Viettel achieves world's highest autonomous network certification
BANGKOK - Viettel has become the first Vietnamese telecom operator to achieve Level 4 Autonomous Network certification, the highest level currently recognised by the global telecoms industry.
The certification was awarded by the TM Forum at Innovate Asia 2026 in Bangkok, Thailand, for solutions developed and commercially deployed by Viettel's engineers.
The two certified functions, mobile network coverage optimisation and energy optimisation, are operated by Viettel Networks Corporation.
TM Forum's independent panel assessed the solutions using real-world operational data and international evaluation criteria.
Autonomous networks can monitor, analyse, make decisions and resolve issues independently, while human operators set objectives and maintain safety controls.
TM Forum's framework has six levels, from Level 0, which relies on manual operations, to Level 5, representing full autonomy.
As Level 5 has yet to be assessed under an established standard, Level 4 is currently the highest recognised level.
Viettel achieved a perfect score of 4.0 for coverage optimisation under the latest assessment framework, surpassing the 3.7 scores of international operators.
It also joined a small group of operators certified at Level 4 for energy optimisation.
Its system continuously monitors network quality nationwide and can detect and address weak-signal areas within hours, rather than waiting for customer complaints or lengthy testing campaigns.
At major events, adjustments can be made in about two minutes, increasing network capacity by more than 3 per cent using existing infrastructure.
For energy optimisation, the system adjusts base-station operations according to demand, reducing power consumption during off-peak hours and restoring capacity when network quality deteriorates.
The solution helps cut electricity costs and emissions.
Viettel said developing its own solutions gives it control over algorithms, data and operations, while reducing reliance on foreign technology providers.
Its coverage optimisation system cost less than one-tenth of an equivalent solution from an international supplier.
George Glass, TM Forum's chief technology officer, said Viettel was the first operator globally to achieve Level 4 in both scenarios under the latest standards.

"This achievement puts Viettel among the world's leading operators in commercially deployed autonomous network capabilities, delivering real operational value and improving customer experience," he said.
Lê Quang Hiếu, deputy general director of Viettel Networks Corporation, said the certification marked the shift of autonomous networking from a strategic direction to an operational capability.
Viettel aims to bring its entire network to Level 4 by 2030 and advance to Level 5 in suitable areas.

It plans to expand autonomous capabilities to fixed broadband, transmission and core networks, while developing telecom-specific AI models and digital twins to test changes in simulated environments before deployment.
The company is also working with TM Forum to develop metrics for autonomous network value and share operational results with the global telecoms community. - VNS
